title: One Live Payment Plan per Patient
content:
**Patient Payment Plans — Terms and Conditions, clause on plans held at one time**

1. **Limit.** A patient may have only one (1) live payment plan at a time. A *live* plan is a plan whose status is pending acceptance, active, past due or defaulted. Plans that are paid off or cancelled remain on file as history and are not live.
2. **No second plan.** A patient who already has a live plan cannot be offered a second one.
3. **New invoices.** A new eligible invoice is added to the live plan where the rule on adding invoices allows it, and otherwise waits until that plan ends.
4. **Basis of the check.** Whether a patient already has a live plan is read from the company's payment-plan records for that patient — the plans on file under the patient and their status — before a plan is offered; the patient's own account of their plans does not decide it.

## The limit by plan status

| Status of an existing plan of the patient | Counts as live | A new plan may be offered |
|---|---|---|
| Pending acceptance | Yes | No |
| Active | Yes | No |
| Past due | Yes | No |
| Defaulted | Yes | No |
| Paid off | No | Not prevented by this clause |
| Cancelled | No | Not prevented by this clause |

## Illustrations (hypothetical patients)

- A patient whose only plan on file was paid off last year and who now owes a new invoice is not blocked by this clause; the paid-off plan is history.
- A patient whose plan defaulted and has not been reinstated still holds a live plan, so no second plan can be offered while that plan stays in the defaulted status.
- A patient with an offer still pending acceptance holds a live plan; a further offer cannot be made alongside it.
- A patient with an active plan and a new eligible invoice: the invoice goes onto the active plan where the add-invoice rule allows; where it does not, the invoice waits until the active plan ends.
